newsitem.title: CANADA: Royal Bank chairman says U.S. too pricey.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank chairman says U.S. too pricey.

text.p: Royal Bank of Canada chairman John Cleghorn said on Wednesday that Canada's biggest bank continued to look for an acquisition in the United States, but that the asking price was often too high.
Cleghorn told reporters that soaring stock prices made a move into the United States very expensive.

"Indeed in some sectors of wealth management, some of the asking prices have gone right out of sight. So the discussions don't take very long," Cleghorn said during a telephone conference call. He said the bank was not currently involved in any talks.

Royal Bank's 1996 acquisitions included the C$480 million purchase of investment banker Richardson Greenshields of Canada Ltd, the acquisition of Toronto-Dominion Bank's wealth and custody businesses, and a small Canadian insurance firm. Cleghorn predicted the bank will do more niche-type acquisitions in Canada next year.
Royal Bank earlier reported a record C$1.43 billion annual profit for the year ended October 31.
Cleghorn declined to give a specific profit forecast for 1997, but he added "we try to attain a minimum of an increase of 10 percent (earnings per share), year-over-year."
Cleghorn said he expected the bank's return on equity to remain within its 16-18 percent target range in the intermediate period.
Royal Bank's return on equity, a key measure of profitability, rose 100 basis points to 17.6 percent in 1996.
